① OBSERVED, measured on the installed 0.74.0 binary in an isolated scratch store (the handlers are unchanged on origin/main 6329079):
- `create_node` wrote Decision dec:m1 with status=accepted: reply {node, loop_hint}, no refusal, no note, and no AUTHORED_BY approver.
- `create_nodes` wrote Requirement status=accepted and DesignRule enforced=true, the same way.
- `import_graph` of a document holding an accepted Decision with no approver edge reported {nodes_written: 3, edges_written: 1}, with nothing distinguishing it from the signed one beside it.
- apply_merge was read in code, not run: it writes the merged state through the same store calls with no settle check.
EXPECTED: the rule the typed tools follow since #628. A settle with no approver is refused (constructors) or recorded with the NOBODYS_NAME note (setters).
NOT AFFECTED: the nine typed tools in crates/reflow2-mcp/src/settles.rs.

② PRECEDENT, searched in child-reflow2 and flo2:
- fact:collapse-decision-settles-a-decision-with-no-approver-and-says-nothing-2026-09-28 listed these four writers and was left open for them by #628.
- cap:an-exposed-server-establishes-who-is-calling-before-intent-can-be-settled (#616 fix 4, planned) maps the core choke point: create_node and create_edge compare stored against new.
- flo2's gateway fact about signing: a settle was keyed by tool and argument name.

③ CANDIDATES from the bones:
(a) Intent/allocation: the rule was scoped to the typed doors.
(b) The generic writers deliberately bypass validation, as an escape hatch.
(c) The Python gate (tools/check_intent_authority.py settles_intent) is the intended catch, after the fact.
(d) The observation is wrong, and something downstream refuses.

④⑤ MEASURED:
- (d) is refuted: the stored node reads accepted, and detect_defects raises only orphan_node.
- (c) is real but after the fact, and only in reflow2's OWN CI; a consumer's design runs no such gate.
- (b) is refuted as intent: create_node's description promises merge semantics, not an exemption from the owner's-word rule, and rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word is ENFORCED.
- (a) stands. The capability's description names only typed tools, and #628's table is keyed per tool, so a writer whose status rides inside `props` or a document has no row.

⑥ CLASS: a rule about a STATE CHANGE (intent moves past its landing status) is enforced at the tool doors, one door at a time. Every door added without it (generic, bulk, import, merge) is a way round. The same class was closed for the typed doors on 2026-09-06 and again by #628, and each time it reopened at the next door.
THE FIX AT THE CAUSE:
- ONE core predicate of which node property values settle intent, read by every writer;
- the generic writers go through the same gate: refused when a constructor settles unsigned; reported when an import or merge carries a settle with no approver edge;
- a class test that fails when a served writer can set a settling value without passing through that predicate.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED:
- the Python gate's copy of the predicate agrees today, by reading the code, and it remains a separate copy;
- whether create_edge of an approver edge itself needs a guard (\"unsigning\" by delete_edge) is #616 fix 4's question, not this one.

SCOPE WIDENED, 2026-09-30, on Anthony's word ("record the proper cure in reflow2's generic-writers fix"). The class reaches APPROVER ROLES as well as statuses.

An AUTHORED_BY edge carrying the approver role is a signature, and on 0.74.0 any write path records one while checking only that the named Contributor exists. Measured on an isolated 0.74.0 store: create_edge AUTHORED_BY {roles:[approver]} naming another contributor succeeds, and so does acknowledge_gaps with a per-item approver. Main has since added draw_edges (#629), whose authored_by items are one more such path.

A hosting gateway, flo2.io, had to CONTAIN this at its front door (flo2 #105, deployed 2026-09-30) by scanning every call's arguments for an approval naming anyone but the signed-in person. That scan retires when this cure ships.

THE PROPER CURE, which belongs in this package (R-S2):
(1) A signature is checked WHERE IT IS WRITTEN, never per tool. That means the store's AUTHORED_BY write, the single point #632 already stamps with the acting agent, and a status leaving its landing through ANY writer, through the one settle table this package adds (intent.rs).
(2) What it is checked AGAINST follows the SETTLED ruling dec:idea-authentication-is-somebody-elses-layer-and-the-line-is-the-contributor-id, option (e):
- local (stdio, --shared, loopback --http) is unchanged;
- on an exposed or registry-served engine, "every AUTHORED_BY a call writes (author or approver) is for that contributor, and a call naming anyone else is refused". The contributor is the one verified from the Bearer token, or the one named by a declared trusted gateway such as flo2's.
(3) The class test drives EVERY served write tool, including bulk forms and nested items, enumerated from the served surface, never by argument name. flo2's old check shows why: it was derived from its own list and read passing while the rule was broken.

COORDINATION: the #616 work implements the settled ruling's enforcement for exposed servers. It must enforce at this same write point, or its "refuse a call naming anyone else" inherits the door-list blind spot this fact describes.

2026-09-30, THE STATUS HALF SHIPPED in reflow2 #635 (squash 3a14696). The parks writer says whether its ruling takes effect. The class test is crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/every_writer_settles_through_one_rule.rs, with its writer list read off the served surface.

THE APPROVER-ROLE HALF IS STILL OWED. It is (1)-(3) above for AUTHORED_BY approver edges: a check at the store's AUTHORED_BY write (#632's point) against dec:idea-authentication-is-somebody-elses-layer-and-the-line-is-the-contributor-id (e). Its class test drives every served write tool, bulk forms and nested items included. #635 does not include it, and the PR body says so. It follows in the next PR (R-S3), coordinated with the #616 work. flo2 #105's containment stays until then.
